We need to read the problem statement carefully. We have an array `nums` of positive integers (length n). In each operation, we can remove the last element of the array and add it to your collection. So we can only pop from the end (like a stack). Initially, the collection is empty. We need to collect elements 1 through k (i.e., need to have at least one occurrence of each integer from 1..k) in the collection. The question: minimum number of operations (i.e., pop operations from the end of the array) needed to ensure that the collected multiset contains all integers 1..k at least once.

We are guaranteed that it's possible (the input is generated such that you can collect elements 1..k). Since we only pop from the end, the process is: We start at index n-1, and we consider the suffix of the array as we pop elements; the collection after t operations consists of the last t elements (in reverse order of popping? Actually each popped element is added to collection; order of addition matters maybe not). We just need that among the last t elements, the set of values seen contains all numbers 1..k.

Thus we need to find the smallest t (0 <= t <= n) such that the suffix of length t (the last t elements of nums) contains all numbers 1..k at least once. Because we can pop exactly those t elements (from the end). Each operation pops the last element; after t operations, we have popped exactly the last t elements (the suffix). So we need minimal t such that the suffix of length t contains all numbers from 1..k. Equivalent to find the furthest left position i (0-indexed) such that the subarray nums[i:] (suffix from i to n-1) contains all numbers 1..k. Then answer = n - i (the length of suffix). Or we can think scanning from right to left, keep a set of needed numbers (1..k) and count how many distinct needed numbers have been seen; we stop when we have seen all k numbers; the number of elements processed (from the right) is answer.

Thus solution: iterate from the end of nums backwards, maintain a set seen (or a boolean array of size k+1). For each element x = nums[i], if 1 <= x <= k, add to seen. When size of seen == k, break; answer = n
